newsitem.title: USA: Marvel debt off amid Chapter 11, no trades [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT].
newsitem.headline: Marvel debt off amid Chapter 11, no trades [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT].

text.p: Bonds backed by shares of Marvel Entertainment Group dipped almost three points on Friday after three Marvel holding companies filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, traders said.
Marvel Holding Inc's "old" bonds were bid at 19 at mid-morning compared with a 21-1/2 bid late on Thursday, traders said. One source said bonds were offered at 21.
Trade for the debt was stagnant ahead of the opening of the stock on the New York Stock Exchange, traders said. Shares of Marvel closed at 2-3/8 on Thursday.

"There should be some trades but they'll be small with people really just testing the waters," said one distressed debt trader. "The stock is probably a little weaker and the bonds will probably trade around 20."
Another trader said the move came as no surprise.

Marvel Holdings, Marvel (Parent) Holdings and Marvel III Holdings on Friday said they filed voluntary petitions for reorganization under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code in a Delaware Court. At the same time, Andrews Group said it signed a definitive merger agreement with Toy Biz, which is dependent on Marvel's reorganization.
Andrews also said it plans to make a $365 million equity investment in Marvel under the proposed Marvel reorganization.
(Corrects to make clear that Andrews will make equity investment in Marvel, not that it will acquire Marvel).
